description: Issue #1080: RequestBindingPolicy.Classify's NoWritableTarget carve-out is new security-relevant logic this PR introduced -- it decides which rejection reasons the two controller RedoUpdateModel implementations are allowed to log at Debug instead of Warning -- and had no mutant covering it until this entry. Neutralizes the shallower-candidate loop inside Classify's last-segment zero-resolution branch (`foreach (var candidate in traversalTypes) { if (candidate.GetMember(segment).Length > 0) { return BindingRejectionReason.UnresolvedIntermediateSegment; } }`, src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs) with a compile-preserving `&& false` on the loop's inner condition (not a deletion, not the outer `members.Length == 0` condition -- this entry is scoped to the loop specifically; see wtmsec867-zero-resolution-guard-neutralize for the mutant covering the outer condition). Without this loop, the only thing left deciding UnresolvedIntermediateSegment vs NoWritableTarget for a last segment that fails to resolve against the DEEPEST traversal type is whatever the (now dead) loop body would have found -- i.e. nothing, so it always falls to `return BindingRejectionReason.NoWritableTarget;`. This matters because PropertyHelper.SetPropertyValue's own intermediate loop (PropertyHelper.cs:523-551) can freeze its traversal type at an EARLIER hop than the deepest one (when a resolved intermediate member's runtime VALUE is null and its type has no public parameterless constructor); Classify's own Type/name-only, value-blind walk cannot see that at analysis time, so a last segment that resolves against a SHALLOWER candidate type already in traversalTypes still represents a possible real write and must stay classified as UnresolvedIntermediateSegment (logged loud), never silently downgraded to NoWritableTarget (logged quiet) just because it also failed against the deepest type. Checked against Classify_LastSegmentUnresolvedAgainstDeepestType_ButResolvesAgainstShallowerType_ReturnsUnresolvedIntermediateSegment -- the test this PR added for exactly this shape: fixture ShallowChainSharedNameVM declares `Shared` directly on the SOURCE type (traversal depth 0) and a nested `Hop` property of type DeepHopTarget (depth 1, no `Shared` member at all); the key 'Hop.Shared' resolves 'Hop' cleanly (advancing tempType to DeepHopTarget and adding it to traversalTypes) then fails to resolve 'Shared' against DeepHopTarget, the deepest type, while it DOES resolve against ShallowChainSharedNameVM, the shallower candidate already in traversalTypes. With the loop neutralized, Classify returns NoWritableTarget instead of UnresolvedIntermediateSegment for this key, which is what turns the Assert.AreEqual red. Confirmed by running the red test directly against the mutant patch (not reasoned about in the abstract): 'Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<UnresolvedIntermediateSegment>. Actual:<NoWritableTarget>. ...' -- proving this PR's own new test really does pin the behaviour it claims to pin, not merely appearing to. The green control, IsPathAllowed_SearcherDotCustomFilterField_ReturnsTrue, resolves 'Searcher' then 'ZipCode' cleanly at every hop (members.Length is never 0 for either segment), so it never enters the members.Length==0 branch at all, let alone this loop -- fully decoupled from the mutated line, not merely unaffected for this specific input.
target_symbol: RequestBindingPolicy.Classify(Type, string, string) -- the `foreach (var candidate in traversalTypes) { if (candidate.GetMember(segment).Length > 0) { return BindingRejectionReason.UnresolvedIntermediateSegment; } }` shallower-candidate loop inside the last-segment zero-resolution branch
red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against a clean checkout with the mutant patch applied (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first), from the TRX <ErrorInfo><Message> node run_mutant.py itself parses: "Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<UnresolvedIntermediateSegment>. Actual:<NoWritableTarget>. 'Shared' resolves against the SOURCE type ShallowChainSharedNameVM (a shallower type already in the traversal chain) even though it does not resolve against the deepest type DeepHopTarget — a frozen-type write is therefore possible and this must stay loud, not be reclassified as NoWritableTarget.". Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant wtmsec867-nowritabletarget-shallower-candidate-guard-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
